title: Robotic Production of Cancer Cell Spheroids with an Aqueous Two-phase System for Drug Testing
protocol: Weigh 0.5 g of polyethylene glycol (PEG) with MW: 35,000.
Add PEG to 9.5 ml of complete growth medium in a sterile 15 ml conical tube to prepare 10 ml of 5% (w/v) aqueous PEG phase.
Weigh 0.128 g of dextran (DEX) with MW: 500,000.
Add DEX to 0.872 ml of complete growth medium in a sterile 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube to prepare 1 ml of 12.8% (w/v) aqueous DEX phase.
Vortex the PEG solution for about 1 min to dissolve the polymer.
Vortex the DEX solution for about 1 min to dissolve the polymer.
Keep both solutions in a water bath at 37 °C for 1 hr to ensure dissolution and homogenous mixtures.
Load the PEG phase solution into a sterile, plastic syringe.
Pass the PEG solution through a syringe filter of 0.2 µm pore size to remove impurities.
Fill the syringe with the PEG solution.
Place the filled syringe in the insert of the filter on top of a conical tube.
Push the solution through the filter using force, experiencing resistance normally.
Pipette 10 µl of the DEX phase solution and dilute it in 10 µl of medium to result in 6.4% (w/v) DEX phase solution.
Aspirate 100 µl of the PEG phase solution and dispense it into a Petri dish.
Dispense 0.5 µl of the 6.4% (w/v) DEX phase solution into the PEG phase solution.
Visually confirm successful ATPS formation by observing a DEX drop under a microscope.
Store stock aqueous PEG and DEX phase solutions in 4°C until use.
Grow cancer cells of interest to a 90%-100% confluent monolayer.
Use DMEM containing 10% FBS, 1% glutamine, and 1% antibiotic for MDA-MB-157 breast cancer cells.
Harvest cells using a cell dissociation buffer according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Load the cell suspension into a 15 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the tube for 5 min at 173.3 x g.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 ml of complete growth medium.
Count cells using a hemocytometer to determine the required number for desired spheroid cell density.
Centrifuge cells for a second time for 5 min at 173.3 x g.
Resuspend cells in an appropriate volume of growth medium to achieve the desired cell density.
Add an equal volume of 12.8% (w/v) aqueous DEX phase solution to the cell suspension.
Thoroughly mix the cell suspension to ensure uniform distribution and mixing of DEX solution.
Gently pipette up and down to prevent bubble formation.
Grow MDA-MB-157 human breast cancer cells and human fibroblasts to a 90%-100% confluent monolayer.
Harvest each cell type using a cell dissociation buffer according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Centrifuge each suspension for 5 min at 173.3 x g in a 15 ml conical tube and aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend cells of each conical tube in 1 ml of complete growth medium.
Load each cell type separately onto a hemocytometer to count them.
Calculate the required number of each cell type for a desired ratio of cancer cells to supporting cells in co-cultured spheroids.
Add the correct volume from the suspension of fibroblasts to the cancer cells suspension to achieve a desired cell ratio, such as 50 cancer cells to 1 fibroblast.
Centrifuge the conical tube containing the mixed cell suspension for 5 min at 173.3 x g.
Resuspend cells in an appropriate volume to result in a final density comprising equal volumes of growth medium and the 12.8% (w/v) aqueous DEX phase solution.
Gently pipette the resulting cell suspension up and down to ensure homogeneity of the suspension.
Coat non-treated, round-bottom 96-well plates with 1% (w/v) Pluronic at 37 °C for 24 hr.
Dispense 50 µl of the filtered 5% (w/v) aqueous PEG phase into each well of a 96-well plate.
Mix the cell suspension and add 20 µl of the suspension to every other well from one column of a 384-well plate.
Turn on the liquid handler and home the pipetting head to register coordinates.
Compile a previously defined protocol to ensure labware and parameters are defined correctly.
Place the source plate, the destination plate, and pipette tip boxes at defined positions on the workstation of the liquid handler.
Load one column of barrels from the pipetting head with mixing pipette tips (8 tips) from the workstation.
Mix the cell suspension in wells of the source plate.
Select a mixing volume smaller than the cell suspension volume to avoid bubble formation.
Eject tips into an empty waste tips box.
Load one column of barrels from the pipetting head with 10 µl dispensing pipette tips.
Aspirate 0.3 µl of the cell suspension from the source plate into each pipette tip.
Dispense the cell suspension into wells of one column of the destination plate.
Use a dispense height of 0.5 mm and a dispense flow rate smaller than 1 µl/sec.
Repeat steps until the column-by-column printing into the entire destination plate is complete.
Carefully remove the destination plate from the workstation surface.
Place the destination plate in a humid incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Maintain the plate horizontal when carrying it into the incubator to avoid disrupting DEX phase drops containing cells.
Incubate the plate for 24 hr to allow aggregation of cells into spheroids within the DEX phase drop.
Visually confirm spheroid formation in 96-well plates after 24 hours.
Image wells for measurement of size of spheroids by averaging the smallest and largest diameters of each spheroid.
Prepare a stock solution of a desired drug by dissolving it in a solvent recommended by the manufacturer at a predetermined solubility concentration.
Protect the stock solution of the drug from light if the drug is light-sensitive.
Using the serial dilution technique, prepare diluted drug concentrations with cell culture medium from the stock solution prepared in the previous step.
Add 50 µl of drug solution to each well.
Use spheroids from two columns of a 96-well plate (n=16) for each concentration.
In control wells, add only 50 µl of fresh culture medium to the existing 50 µl of the aqueous PEG phase.
Incubate spheroids with the drug for 48 hours at 37 °C and 5% CO2, protected from light.
Prepare fresh dilutions of the drug at desired concentrations after 48 hours of incubation.
Add 50 µl of fresh drug solution to each well containing the initial drug concentration.
Incubate spheroids with the renewed drug for another 48 hours at 37 °C and 5% CO2, protected from light.
Measure the total volume of medium in one well by manual pipetting after 48 hours of renewed incubation.
Calculate the volume of cell viability reagent as 10% concentration of the total well volume.
Add this calculated volume of cell viability reagent to each well.
Incubate the plate with the added cell viability reagent for 6 hours at 37 °C, protected from light.
Place the plate in a micro-plate reader.
Read the fluorescence signal at 560 nm excitation and 590 nm emission wavelengths.
Calculate the percent viability of cells in spheroids by normalizing the fluorescent signal from treated wells to that of control wells.
